overview: A flame sensor looks almost identical to the simple IR obstacle sensor — same small board, same comparator chip, same dark IR-receiver dome — but its photodiode is specifically tuned to the infrared wavelength range that flames emit strongly (roughly 760-1100nm), letting it detect fire at a distance even in normal ambient light. It's a presence/absence detector, not a temperature sensor: it answers 'is there a flame-like IR source in view,' not 'how hot is it,' and like any IR-based sensor it can be fooled by other strong IR sources (direct sunlight, incandescent bulbs) giving false positives.
simpleSummary: A sensor tuned to spot the infrared light a flame gives off, so it can detect fire nearby.

specifications.detectionRange: ~20cm - 100cm depending on flame size, adjustable sensitivity via trimpot

pinMap.name: AOUT
pinMap.function: Analog output — voltage varies with detected IR intensity.

pinMap.name: DOUT
pinMap.function: Digital threshold output — typically LOW when flame-range IR is detected above the trimpot-set threshold.
pinMap.gotcha: Bright sunlight or incandescent bulbs can trigger false positives since they also emit strongly in the near-IR range this sensor watches.

useCases.title: Fire detection alarm
useCases.scenario: Trigger a buzzer or notification when a flame is detected within range.

useCases.title: Fire-fighting robot (competition-style)
useCases.scenario: Steer a small robot toward a detected candle flame and trigger a fan/extinguisher mechanism.

oftenConfusedWith: MQ-2 gas sensor (detects smoke/gas composition, not flame IR signature)
IR obstacle sensor (same form factor, different wavelength tuning)
oftenUpgradedTo: Thermal camera modules for actual temperature-based fire detection
